The exercise ECG shows dynamic QRS widening and new T-wave inversions in recovery, strongly indicating exercise-induced myocardial ischemia. Normal BNP, preserved LVEF, no wall motion abnormalities, and resting narrow QRS argue against heart failure. Unremarkable exam and ischemic ECG changes make pulmonary disease or deconditioning less likely. Aortic valve sclerosis with mild regurgitation is only a minor contributor. Thus, coronary artery disease with exercise-induced ischemia is the most probable cause; coronary angiography or perfusion imaging is needed for definitive confirmation.
